My password is the last eight digits of pi.
I ran three miles today. Then I remembered where I parked.
I don’t trust stairs. They’re always up to something.
My dog used to chase people on a bike. I had to take the bike away.
I’m on a seafood diet. I see food and I question my choices.
Autocorrect is my ducking nemesis.
My ceiling fan is my biggest supporter. It has never once looked down on me.
I water my plants with the confidence of a man who has never kept one alive.
Why did the chicken cross the road? Because the crosswalk signal changed and it was safe to proceed.
A horse walks into a bar. Several patrons leave, concerned about the lack of health code enforcement.
Knock knock. Who’s there? A courier with a package you have to sign for.
I told my therapist about my fear of speed bumps. She said I would get over it. I have not; I still drive around them.
Every office has one microwave and a queue of people pretending they don’t mind waiting. The fish guy knows. The fish guy has always known.
The meeting could have been an email. The email could have been a message. The message could have been nothing at all, which is what everyone wanted.
There is a specific age where you stop looking at the price of avocados and start looking at the price of avocados very carefully.
You never really own a gym membership. You rent a small monthly reminder of the person you meant to become.
The fastest way to find a bug in your code is to demonstrate it working to someone else.
Airports are the only place where a cinnamon roll at six in the morning counts as a personal decision rather than a cry for help.
Grocery self-checkout is the only job I have ever been promoted into without an interview.
My phone knows me better than my family does, mostly because my family has never once asked what I searched at two in the morning.
I finally achieved work-life balance: I am equally bad at both.
The productivity app I bought to stop procrastinating has been sitting unopened for four months, which I consider a kind of consistency.
Our team won an award for efficiency. The ceremony ran three hours.
I have started introducing my houseplants at parties. So far only the fern has made a good impression, and frankly it is carrying the rest of them.
My neighbour built a fence so tall that it now has its own weather system. On Tuesdays it drizzles on his side only, and on Thursdays a small cloud sits above the gate and refuses to move until someone acknowledges it.
The moon landing was faked, but only the parking. They landed fine; getting the spot was the hard part.
I taught my cat to fetch, and now she brings me things I never threw, which I have decided not to investigate.
Every time I open the fridge, the light judges me. I have started opening it in the dark to level the field.
My commute is so long that I have watched two coworkers get hired, promoted and married while I sat in the same left-turn lane.
The line at the DMV moved so slowly that I aged into a different bracket of the form I was holding.
My grandmother’s soup portions assume you have brought four friends, a thermos, and a plan for the winter.
I have so many browser tabs open that my laptop has started rationing electricity like a small nation in crisis.
I am not saying I am bad at cooking, but my smoke alarm has a favourite recipe.
I went to the gym once in January. The staff still send me letters like an estranged relative.
My résumé says “detail-oriented” in two different fonts.
I speak three languages: English, sarcasm, and a version of Spanish that only works on menus.
What do you call a factory that makes okay products? A satisfactory.
Why don’t scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything, and frankly so do scientists when the grant deadline is close.
Why did the developer go broke? He used up all his cache.
What did the ocean say to the shore? Nothing. It just waved, which is more than my neighbour does.
Why do bees have sticky hair? Because they use honeycombs.
A man tells his doctor he broke his arm in two places. The doctor advises him to stop going to those places. He now only goes to one place, and he is much happier and slightly more bored.
A woman walks into a hardware store and asks for a hammer that does not judge her. The clerk hands her a rubber mallet and says it is the closest thing they carry. She uses it on a shelf for six months. The shelf holds.
My uncle spent thirty years perfecting a recipe for chili he never wrote down. At the funeral we tried to reconstruct it from memory and ended up inventing four new chilis, none of which were his, all of which he would have hated.
Waiter: “How did you find your steak?” Diner: “I moved the potato and there it was.”
Manager: “We need this by Friday.” Me: “Which Friday?” Manager: “The one that already happened.”
Kid: “Dad, are we there yet?” Dad: “We haven’t left.” Kid: “Are we there yet?”
Three things I learned from my first startup: hire slowly, fire kindly, and never let the person who bought the office beanbag pick the database.
My morning routine: wake up, check phone, regret checking phone, check phone again to confirm the regret.
Packing for a week away: two shirts I will wear, nine shirts I will not, and one shirt that exists purely to make the suitcase look ambitious.
I told my wife she should embrace her mistakes. She gave me a hug. Later she embraced the dog, and I have been thinking about that all week.
My friend said he would tell me a joke about construction, but he is still working on it. The scaffolding has been up for six years.
I asked an AI to write my performance review. It gave me a raise, a promotion, and a warning about my tone in meetings.
Every product I own now has a subscription, including, as of last Tuesday, my toothbrush.
My team’s standup has become a support group where we each describe a dashboard we no longer believe in.
Politics is the only industry where you can fail upward in public and call it a listening tour.
The referee made a call so bad that the crowd briefly united across three decades of rivalry to boo in perfect harmony.
I joined a fantasy league to feel closer to my brother. Now we text more than ever, entirely in insults.
My landlord called the apartment cozy. The estate agent called it efficient. The mouse called it home.
I finally read the terms and conditions. I now legally owe a company in Delaware one weekend a year.
